briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The most critical development of the past 24 hours is the declared ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon, brokered by the US, which was immediately and vehemently rejected by Hezbollah and Iran's IRGC. This rejection has been followed by continued cross-border hostilities, including the death of an IDF officer and a UN peacekeeper.

IRAN
Mohsen Rezai, military advisor to Iran's Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, stated that Trump is attempting to pressure Iran with vague conditions. Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi affirmed Iran's commitment to peace and security but stated that its armed forces are ready to resume war and attack Israel at any moment. Araghchi also thanked regional countries, specifically Saudi Arabia and Qatar, for their mediation efforts with the US, but accused the UAE of participating in military operations against Iran and aligning with Israel. He warned that US bases in regional countries, if used against Iran, would be legitimate targets. Araghchi stated that Iran and Oman would jointly manage the Strait of Hormuz according to international law. Mojtaba Khamenei, in a written message for Imam Khomeini's anniversary, accused the US and Israel of waging a "hybrid war" against Iran, focusing on public resilience and disrupting officials' calculations. Trump claimed that if Iran kills US troops, he would restart the war "very quickly" and asserted that Iran will never acquire nuclear weapons, stating the US had "destroyed" Iran's navy, air force, and leadership. He also claimed Iran agreed to US removal of enriched uranium. The IAEA urged Iran to fully cooperate regarding the fate of its enriched uranium following last year's bombings and allow full inspections. Iran is reportedly accelerating work on the International North-South Transport Corridor and expanding civil nuclear cooperation with Russia, including a $25 billion power plant in Hormozgan.

ISRAEL
An IDF officer, Captain Eitan Shmuel Lemberg (21) of the 75th Battalion, 7th Armored Brigade, was killed by a Hezbollah anti-tank missile north of the Litani River in southern Lebanon. The IDF announced the appointment of Rear Admiral Tal Politis as Israel's next defense attaché to the United States and Brigadier General Barak Hiram to head the Operations Division. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu appointed Brigadier General Guy Markizeno as his military secretary, with a promotion to Major General. Netanyahu visited Shlomi, affirming commitment to northern residents' security despite ongoing alarms. A survey indicated that Benny Gantz's National Unity party leader Gadi Eisenkot has surpassed Netanyahu in suitability for Prime Minister. Israel's Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar announced the opening of an Israeli embassy in Slovenia, marking a new chapter in relations. Tourism entries in May 2026 dropped by 83% compared to May 2023. Home front incidents included two men killed in Yafia, a man shot dead in Tamra, and Lihya Malka Cohen (35), a former policewoman, killed in a car bomb in Ayalon (suspect arrested). Border communities in the Galilee Panhandle experienced rocket and hostile aircraft intrusion alerts. The IDF announced that Mossad provided weapons taken from Hamas and Hezbollah to the Kurds as part of a plan to overthrow the Ayatollah regime in Iran.

GAZA & WEST BANK
The IDF and Shin Bet eliminated top commanders of Hamas's general security mechanism in the Gaza Strip through air and sea strikes. Among those killed were Hassan Labad, the deputy head of the security mechanism, along with Asem Shabir, Abdullah Abu Kaloub, and Mohammed Abu Marek. IDF has called for residents to evacuate the Al-Maghazi refugee camp in central Gaza. Palestinian reports indicated casualties following an Israeli strike on a police point at Al-Shaabiya intersection in Gaza City. Armed Israeli settlers violently beat a Palestinian civilian in Al-Duyuk al-Tahta and set fire to Palestinian farmlands northeast of Ramallah. An indictment was filed against Ibrahim Hilu (46) for holding the body of Staff Sergeant Oron Shaul for Hamas for over 10 years; Shaul's body was eventually recovered based on information from Hilu. In the West Bank, forces from Unit 636 killed a militant who threw Molotov cocktails at an Israeli road near the village of Beitunia.

LEBANON
The US, Israel, and Lebanon announced a ceasefire agreement conditioned on Hezbollah's complete cessation of fire and withdrawal north of the Litani River. However, Hezbollah Secretary-General Sheikh Naim Qassem explicitly rejected the agreement, calling it "shameless" and "disgraceful," and affirmed that northern Israel would not be safe as long as Lebanese villages are attacked. Iran's IRGC also rejected the ceasefire, demanding an immediate halt to Israeli attacks and withdrawal from occupied territories. Hezbollah fired two rockets at IDF forces in southern Lebanon, with one intercepted and the other falling near troops, causing no injuries. An IDF officer, Captain Eitan Shmuel Lemberg, was killed by a Hezbollah anti-tank missile north of the Litani River. Hezbollah also deployed FPV drones, with one reportedly striking a vehicle in the convoy of Northern Command chief Major General Rafi Milo during a visit to southern Lebanon; no injuries were reported. The IDF's Givati Brigade killed a Hezbollah operative north of the Litani and subsequently located a large weapons cache including firearms and a small surface-to-air missile. The Israeli Air Force struck two Hezbollah cells in Tyre and Shaqra. Extensive Israeli airstrikes were reported across southern Lebanon, including Nabatieh, Toulain, Khirbat Silim, Tibnin, Kana, Sarifa, and Libaiya. Mortar shells launched by Hezbollah struck a UNIFIL position in Dibbin, killing Serbian peacekeeper Sergeant Milovan Jovanović and wounding two others. The IDF attributed this fire to Hezbollah, while Hezbollah denied responsibility, calling it a "false claim." The Lebanese army reported that Israeli forces had fully withdrawn from the Dabbin and Blat areas, and Lebanese troops were deploying to reopen the connecting road. The IDF warned residents of southern Lebanon not to travel south of the Zahrani River.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Reports of explosions were heard in Aleppo, Syria. The Iraqi Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces announced the formation of a high central committee, including representatives from Defense, Interior, and the Popular Mobilization Forces, to restrict weapons to state control. The leader of Harakat Hezbollah al-Nujaba rejected calls for disarmament, stating weapons are necessary to defend Iraq's sovereignty against US occupation.

GULF STATES
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with Kuwait's Foreign Minister a day after Iran's attack on Kuwait International Airport with 30 missiles and drones, which resulted in one fatality and 63 injuries. The US State Department issued a security alert for all US citizens in the Middle East, advising them to locate the nearest shelter due to the "potential for hostilities." Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi accused the UAE of using its airspace and territory for US and Israeli operations against Iran, stating that documents prove the UAE's involvement in military operations. He expressed regret that this "war" caused further disagreements with the UAE. Oman is reportedly resisting US pressure to sever ties with Iran, asserting its role as a neutral mediator and its intention to negotiate a joint management system for the Strait of Hormuz with Iran. Four Iranian-flagged oil tankers carrying seven million barrels of oil passed through the Strait of Hormuz, marking the first such transit since April 17 amidst a US blockade. Russia's Foreign Minister Lavrov stated that the US war against Iran is aimed at controlling energy markets.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Ceasefire Rejection:** Hezbollah Secretary-General Sheikh Naim Qassem and Iran's IRGC rejected a US-brokered ceasefire agreement between Israel and Lebanon, citing continued Israeli aggression and demanding full Israeli withdrawal and no links to Hezbollah's presence.
2.  **IDF Officer Killed:** Captain Eitan Shmuel Lemberg (21) was killed by a Hezbollah anti-tank missile in southern Lebanon, north of the Litani River.
3.  **UN Peacekeeper Death:** Mortar shells launched by Hezbollah struck a UNIFIL position in Dibbin, southern Lebanon, killing Serbian peacekeeper Sergeant Milovan Jovanović and wounding two others.
4.  **Hamas Commanders Eliminated:** The IDF and Shin Bet killed top commanders of Hamas's general security mechanism, including Hassan Labad, in Gaza through air and sea strikes.
5.  **Kuwait Airport Attack:** Iran attacked Kuwait International Airport with 30 missiles and drones, resulting in one death and 63 injuries, prompting a US security alert for the Middle East. Iran denied responsibility for hitting the airport terminal.
6.  **Trump's Iran Statements & US House Vote:** President Trump threatened to restart the war if Iran kills US troops and claimed progress in talks, while the US House of Representatives voted to limit his war powers concerning Iran (215-208).
7.  **IDF Appointments:** Rear Admiral Tal Politis was appointed Defense Attaché to the US, Brigadier General Barak Hiram as head of Operations Division, and Brigadier General Guy Markizeno as PM Netanyahu's military secretary.
8.  **Mossad Arming Kurds:** It was revealed that Mossad provided weapons taken from Hamas and Hezbollah to Kurdish forces as part of a plan to overthrow the Ayatollah regime in Iran.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks remain critically high due to Hezbollah's outright rejection of the ceasefire deal, combined with continued cross-border attacks and Israeli retaliatory strikes. The killing of an IDF officer and a UN peacekeeper in southern Lebanon are significant escalations, potentially triggering more severe responses. Trump's "red line" regarding US casualties in Iran could swiftly reignite direct US-Iran conflict. The IAEA's unaddressed concerns regarding Iran's enriched uranium and lack of inspection access further raise proliferation risks. The active flashpoints are primarily southern Lebanon and the Israeli-Lebanese border, with Gaza also remaining volatile. Military postures on all sides, particularly between Israel and Hezbollah, appear poised for continued, possibly intensified, conflict despite diplomatic efforts.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **United States** brokered a ceasefire agreement between Israel and Lebanon, but President Trump simultaneously made strong statements regarding potential military action against Iran, calling the House vote to limit his war powers "unpatriotic." The **US State Department** issued a security alert for the entire Middle East, urging citizens to locate shelters. **Russia's** President Putin called the Ukraine crisis "local" but the Iran situation "global," offering to mediate and claiming close ties with Iran. Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov accused the US of seeking control over energy markets through its conflict with Iran. **Qatar** and **Pakistan** were identified by Iran's Foreign Minister as mediators in de-escalation efforts with the US. **Saudi Arabia's** Foreign Minister held phone discussions with Iran's Foreign Minister, affirming a desire for continued dialogue. The **UAE** was accused by Iran of participating in military operations against Iran and aligning with Israel. The **UN** welcomed the ceasefire announcement but expressed sorrow over the death of a peacekeeper, calling for full implementation of UNSC Resolution 1701. The **EU's** Foreign Policy Chief welcomed the ceasefire as an opportunity to prevent wider war and offered €100 million in aid to Lebanese armed forces.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant contradictions surround the status of the "ceasefire" in Lebanon, with the US, Israel, and Lebanon announcing an agreement while Hezbollah and the IRGC definitively rejected it, indicating a major disconnect in understanding or intent. Claims by President Trump that Iran agreed to US removal of enriched uranium, that Hezbollah contacted the US for a ceasefire, and that the US has "destroyed" Iran's military capabilities lack independent verification and are largely contradicted by Iranian and Hezbollah statements. The reports surrounding the status of Mojtaba Khamenei, including unverified claims of his father's death and his own assumed leadership (from Omid Dana), clash with official Iranian reporting that acknowledges a "Leader شهید" and "new Leader" but implies the current Supreme Leader is alive with security concerns preventing public appearances. CNN's footage showing extensive damage to the USS Gerald R. Ford contradicts initial US Navy claims of minor fire, highlighting potential information obfuscation by US sources. Al Hadath's report of a four-phase US-Iran deal is explicitly dismissed as "100% false" by another source (omid dana), indicating a major reporting gap or deliberate disinformation. The specific details of Mossad providing weapons to Kurds (from Amit Segal) require further independent corroboration. The IDF's warning to southern Lebanese residents not to return, despite Lebanese reports of Israeli withdrawal, suggests a potential for continued military presence or uncertainty. Hezbollah's denial of striking the UNIFIL position, despite IDF's clear attribution, points to propaganda efforts.
